name: IC 5052 (Hubble)
blurb: IC 5052, a barred spiral galaxy turned side-on, seen by Hubble.
label: ic5052trunc-hubble
story: IC 5052 is a barred spiral galaxy turned side-on to us, its disk pressed into a thin blade of stars, with pockets of hot newborn stars along it. Hubble mapped its stars to trace the disk's truncation, the place where a galaxy's starlight suddenly drops off more steeply, as most disk galaxies show.

claims.text: IC 5052 is a barred spiral galaxy
IC 5052 has pockets of hot newborn stars
The program targeted IC 5052 to study its disk truncation
A disk truncation is where the light profile breaks to a steeper drop
Most disk galaxies show a truncation
The truncations are mapped with resolved stars
